"""
CORS: lets a browser app served from another address (for example the Vite dev server on
http://localhost:5173) call this API.

A browser only lets a page read responses from ANOTHER origin when the API says so with CORS headers.
Without them every request from the frontend is blocked by the browser, even though the API is fine.

Choices made here:
  * Only the origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS are allowed (no "*"), so other websites cannot call the API
    from a user's browser.
  * No cookies: the frontend sends its Clerk token in the Authorization header, so credentials stay off.
  * Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* are EXPOSED. Browsers hide all non-standard response headers from
    JavaScript unless they are listed, and the frontend needs Retry-After to show "try again in N seconds".
  * An empty CORS_ORIGINS turns CORS off (the right setting when the frontend is served from the same origin).
"""

ALLOWED_METHODS = ["GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"]
ALLOWED_HEADERS = ["Authorization", "Content-Type"]
EXPOSED_HEADERS = ["Retry-After", "X-RateLimit-Limit", "X-RateLimit-Reset"]


def parse_origins(value: str) -> list[str]:
    """"http://a.com, http://b.com/" -> ["http://a.com", "http://b.com"] (browsers send origins without a trailing slash)."""
    return [origin.strip().rstrip("/") for origin in value.split(",") if origin.strip()]


def cors_options(cors_origins: str) -> dict | None:
    """Keyword arguments for Starlette's CORSMiddleware, or None when no origin is configured."""
    origins = parse_origins(cors_origins)
    if not origins:
        return None
    return {
        "allow_origins": origins,
        "allow_credentials": False,
        "allow_methods": ALLOWED_METHODS,
        "allow_headers": ALLOWED_HEADERS,
        "expose_headers": EXPOSED_HEADERS,
        "max_age": 600,                      # the browser may cache a preflight answer for 10 minutes
    }

    "do not have enough information",
    "not enough information",
    "does not contain enough information",
    "doesn't contain enough information",
    "does not provide enough information",
    "doesn't provide enough information",
    "insufficient information",

    "i don't know",

    True if the answer says the context doesn't contain the answer.
    An answer that cites a source is a real answer, even if it mentions
    "not enough information" about some other detail.

        return False

    text = answer.lower().replace("’", "'")  # curly apostrophe -> '
    return (
        any(phrase in text for phrase in REFUSAL_PHRASES)
        or REFUSAL_PATTERN.search(text) is not None

    )

def add_line_numbers(source: str, chunks: list[Document]) -> list[Document]:
    """
    Adds `start_line` / `end_line` (1-based, inclusive) to each chunk's metadata: the lines of `source` it covers.

    We do not use LangChain's `add_start_index`: measured on repetitive code it gave a wrong offset for 3 of 154
    chunks. Instead we search for each chunk's text ourselves. Chunks arrive in file order and each one starts
    inside (or right after) the previous one, so the search starts after the previous chunk's start and, first,
    only looks as far as the previous chunk's end. If two identical blocks sit inside that window the earlier one
    wins, so a repeated block can be off by one block (never outside the file). A chunk that cannot be found
    simply gets no line numbers.

    Leading/trailing newlines of a chunk are ignored when counting: the splitter keeps the separator, so a chunk
    often starts with the "\n" that ends the PREVIOUS line.
    """
    newline_at = [i for i, char in enumerate(source) if char == "\n"]

    def line_of(index: int) -> int:
        return bisect_left(newline_at, index) + 1   # newlines before this character, plus one

    previous_start, previous_end = -1, 0
    for chunk in chunks:
        text = chunk.page_content
        start = source.find(text, previous_start + 1, previous_end + len(text))
        if start == -1:
            start = source.find(text, previous_start + 1)
        if start == -1:
            continue

        content = text.rstrip("\r\n")
        first = start + (len(text) - len(text.lstrip("\r\n")))
        last = start + len(content) - 1
        if first > last:                      # a chunk made only of newlines
            first = last = start
        chunk.metadata["start_line"] = line_of(first)
        chunk.metadata["end_line"] = line_of(last)
        previous_start, previous_end = start, start + len(text)
    return chunks

"""

  * An empty CORS_ORIGINS turns CORS off (the right setting when the frontend is served from the same origin).
"""

Gemini fallback, free-tier quota; uploads cost embedding work) from one user, a bug or a script.
